title: decompose-ci-hooks-to-go-plugins-and-update-license-headers
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Our presubmit hooks and release preflight are implemented as a mix of bash entrypoints and GitHub Actions composites. This has led to several flakes (subshell quoting, inconsistent PATHs), poor testability, and slow iteration for repo-standard tooling. This PR decomposes core CI hooks into small, versioned Go-based actions (ci-toolchain-bootstrap, ci-lint-adapter, ci-release-smoke) and updates repository license headers to a standard SPDX header for legal compliance.

What changed (high level):
- Introduced a lightweight Go-based action runner under infra/ci/plugins/ that replaces the long-running bash entrypoints. These are intentionally single-responsibility CLIs that read JSON config from stdin for easier testing.
- Bootstrapping: moved toolchain bootstrap logic into ci-toolchain-bootstrap (pins go/node/python versions and provides a hermetic toolcache path). This reduces matrix size by detecting host capabilities at runtime and avoiding unnecessary matrix axes.
- Lint/test adapters: added ci-lint-adapter which normalizes linter invocation across repos and acts as a compatibility shim for legacy configs. This allowed us to simplify the workflow files to a single lint job with sharding hints.
- Release smoke: added ci-release-smoke, a small action used by the release workflow to run a minimal end-to-end smoke test (deploy to staging, run sanity prompts, validate response shape) before signing artifacts.
- License headers: standardized SPDX license headers across changed files and added a simple license-check step to the precommit flow.
- CI changes: updated .github/workflows/ci.yml to use the new actions, trimmed the test matrix by consolidating platform axes, and introduced a fastpath presubmit lane for changes limited to docs and examples.

Why Go actions: Go binaries are hermetic across runners, compile to a single artifact, and are easier to unit test compared to shell scripts. They also avoid frequent quoting and environment issues we saw in bash-based hooks.

Checklist:
- [x] Add Go action sources + build scripts
- [x] Update workflow YAML to use new actions
- [x] Add license header updates and license-check job
- [x] Run full CI and fix resulting lint/test regressions
- [x] Smoke-tested release workflow in staging

Testing notes / validation steps:
1) Local: make -C infra/ci/plugins/ build && ./bin/ci-toolchain-bootstrap --dry-run
2) CI: confirm GitHub Actions 'ci/build' and 'ci/lint' pass (they now exercise the Go binaries via action wrapper)
3) Release smoke: tested on staging tag v2026.02.28-smoke and validated failure/fallback behavior

Related work: ENG-4821 (ci-era modernization), ENG-4999 (release reliability). Also follows-up on past bash-to-go experiments in infra/ci (see PRs: refactor/ci-go-experiment).
